skill_title: Relate wavelength, frequency, period and wave speed for transverse waves

items.question: What is the wavelength of a transverse wave?
items.expectedAnswer: The distance of one complete wave, e.g. crest to crest.
items.explanation: One wavelength is one full wave — measured crest-to-crest or trough-to-trough.
options: The distance of one complete wave, e.g. crest to crest.
The distance from a crest to the next trough.
The height of a crest above the rest position.

items.question: What is the frequency of a wave?
items.expectedAnswer: The number of complete waves passing a point per second.
items.explanation: Frequency is waves per second, measured in hertz (Hz).
options: The time for one complete wave.
The number of complete waves passing a point per second.

items.question: What is the period of a wave?
items.expectedAnswer: The time taken for one complete wave to pass a point.
items.explanation: Period T is the time for one full wave, measured in seconds.
options: The number of waves per second.
The time taken for one complete wave to pass a point.

items.question: Which equation links period and frequency?
items.explanation: Period and frequency are reciprocals: T = 1/f.

items.question: Which equation gives the speed of a wave?
items.explanation: Wave speed = frequency × wavelength: v = fλ.

items.question: A wave has a frequency of 5 Hz. What is its period?
A wave has a period of 0.25 s. What is its frequency?
A wave has frequency 2 Hz and wavelength 3 m. What is its speed?
Does increasing the amplitude of a wave change its wave speed (on the same medium)?
items.expectedAnswer: No — amplitude does not affect wave speed.
items.explanation: Wave speed depends on the medium, not the amplitude.
options: Yes — bigger amplitude means faster waves.
Yes — bigger amplitude means slower waves.
No — amplitude does not affect wave speed.

items.question: On a transverse wave, what is the amplitude?
items.expectedAnswer: The maximum displacement from the rest position (crest height).
items.explanation: Amplitude is the greatest displacement from rest, e.g. the height of a crest.
options: The maximum displacement from the rest position (crest height).
The number of crests per second.

items.question: A wave travels at 12 m·s⁻¹ with a wavelength of 4 m. What is its frequency?
items.explanation: v = fλ ⇒ f = v/λ = 12/4 = 3 Hz.

items.question: A wave has a speed of 20 m·s⁻¹ and a frequency of 5 Hz. What is its wavelength?
A wave has a period of 0.5 s and a wavelength of 6 m. What is its speed?
A water wave makes 10 complete waves pass a point in 5 s. What is its frequency?
items.explanation: f = number of waves/time = 10/5 = 2 Hz.

items.question: A wave of frequency 4 Hz travels at 8 m·s⁻¹. How far does one wave (one wavelength) stretch?
If the frequency of a wave doubles while the wave speed stays the same, what happens to its wavelength?
items.explanation: From v = fλ at constant v, f and λ are inversely related: double f ⇒ half λ.

items.question: The distance from one crest to the next crest of a wave is 0.5 m, and 6 waves pass each second. What is the wave speed?
A wave has period 0.1 s. How many complete waves pass a point in 2 s?
items.explanation: f = 1/T = 10 Hz; in 2 s the number of waves = f × t = 10 × 2 = 20.

items.question: Two waves travel on the same rope. Wave X has a longer wavelength than wave Y but the same speed. Which has the higher frequency?
items.explanation: At the same speed, v = fλ means shorter λ ⇒ higher f, so wave Y has the higher frequency.

items.question: A transverse wave on a string has a crest-to-trough vertical distance of 8 cm. What is its amplitude?
items.explanation: Crest-to-trough = twice the amplitude, so amplitude = 8/2 = 4 cm.
